rationale: Round 0 built and passed cleanly, so the weights are shifted toward stronger obfuscation: SecurityGain/DiversityGain are raised across all passes to widen per-function selection, since this loop_unroll benchmark's four large hot functions (_Z2[6-9]test_*_loop_unroll*, ~2KB each) give flattening (FLA) and bogus control flow (BCF) high-value structured control flow to obscure, while SPLIT stays cheap and low-risk to compound with FLA by fragmenting blocks first. RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights on BCF/IBR/ICALL are kept moderately high (0.5-0.7) so the selector still applies them selectively rather than saturating the hot loops, preserving acceptable overhead on this execution-bound benchmark. IBR and ICALL retain the highest CorrectnessRisk weights (0.4) because indirect dispatch on C++ heavy-abstraction code (Stepanov/function-object templates, constant folding) risks call-site misresolution, while SUB remains near-free to apply everywhere. IGV is kept at a balanced profile to interleave global variables and diversify data layout without destabilizing the template-heavy code.
